Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
Heard Shri Mohd Fahim, learned Counsel for the applicant and Shri Ashwani Kumar Singh, learned A.G.A for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant seeking bail in F.I.R. No. 42 of 2022 under Sections 376, 377 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station-Saadatganj,
District-Lucknow.
This is the second bail application.
The first bail application of the accused-applicant has been rejected by this Court vide order dated 24.11.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.6632 of 2022.

sentences.text: 1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2. The present bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant seeking bail in FIR No.42 of 2022 under Sections 376, 377, 506 IPC, Police Station Saadatganj, Lucknow.
3. Allegation against the accused-applicant is that the accused-applicant enticed the prosecutrix and promised to marry her.

On the pretext of marrying the prosecutrix,
he established physical relation with her.
When the prosecutrix put pressure on the accused-applicant to marry her, the accused-applicant said that unless she converted herself to Islam, he would not perform the marriage with her.
It is further said that the accused-applicant had also clicked some indecent photographs of the prosecutrix and threatened her that he would make the photographs viral in the social media.
The prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Sections 164 Cr.P.C. had made several allegations against the accused-applicant.

4. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the fact that the accused-applicant had allegedly put a condition of conversion on the prosecutrix to marry her and on the pretext of marriage, he had established physical relation,
besides other allegations, this Court does not consider it to be a fit case for enlarging the accused-applicant on bail at this stage.
This bail application is thus, rejected.

Trial Court is directed to proceed with the trial expeditiously and record evidence of the prosecutrix preferably within a period of 2 months from the date a certified copy of this order is produced before it subject to full cooperation by the accused.
After recording of the statement of the prosecutrix, the accused-applicant may revive the bail plea, if he is so advised.
5.Let a copy of this order be forwarded to the learned trial court for necessary compliance."
The prosecutrix has been examined in the trial court and she has not supported the prosecution case and has been declared hostile.
The prosecutrix was major so was the accused-applicant.
It was a consensual relationship between them.

It is well settled in the case of Deepak Gulati vs. State of Haryana reported in (2013) 7 SCC 675, if the promise is not false and has not been made with sole intention to seduce the prosecutrix and later on the marriage could not materialized, the offences under Section 376 would not be deducted.

entities.text: Deepak Gulati vs. State of Haryana reported in (2013) 7 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the law laid down in Deepak Gulati (Supra) and the facts and circumstances of the present case, I find it appropriate to enlarge/release the accused-applicant on bail.
In view thereof, the present second bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: Let the applicant-Mohammad Amir, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.

In case of default of this condition,
it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A IPC.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1)
opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause,
then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
